name: Voltrox
description: Attention-grabbing: yellow and magenta, ink borders, slapped stickers, punch-in cuts
guide: Fast: something changes every 2–3 s (punch-in, word pop, sticker or full-frame card). The camera already punches in every ~2 s.
Open on a centered stacked Hook Card (title on halftone, a phrase on the seam, speaker below), then cut back to full frame.
Word pops sit in the lower third, tilted, 2–4 words; a sticker in the top corner for every number.
Full-frame yellow cards for lists and prices, then straight back to the speaker.

name: Snipwork
description: Paper craft: ransom-note cut-out letters, torn paper, stop-motion, xerox grain
guide: Handmade: everything moves on twos (stop-motion) and slaps down; the camera steps in like a re-framed photo.
Open with the speaker as a taped photo under a ransom-note title (Hook Card collage).
Headlines are ransom notes, one letter per beat or word; keep them short (1–3 words).
Cards are torn paper with masking tape over a kraft backdrop; cut back to the speaker between them.
Captions are cut-out words on scraps; keep 2–3 words per line.

name: Doodlepad
description: Whiteboard: grid paper, handwriting, marker highlights, a slow drift
guide: Explainer pace: an overlay every 4–6 s; the camera drifts in slowly on each clip.
Split Hook Card with a torn grid-paper top for the title.
Marker-highlight one word per phrase; circle numbers with a drawn sticker.
Notebook cards for lists and quotes, taped to the page.

name: Phosphor
description: Terminal: green on black, typed text, scanlines, glitch cuts
guide: Builder pace: an overlay every 3–5 s; everything types in, the camera glitch-jumps on beats.
Open with the speaker inside a terminal window under a typed title (Hook Card window).
Terminal windows for lists, quotes and numbers; full-frame CRT cards between speaker shots.
Captions as terminal lines in the lower third, the spoken word inverted.
Keep text lowercase and short, like commands.

name: Hexwire
description: Cyberpunk: neon magenta and cyan, glitch type, HUD frames, a neon grid
guide: Fast and glitchy: an overlay every 2–4 s; the camera tears sideways on beats.
Open with the speaker framed in HUD brackets under a neon title (Hook Card hud).
Neon cards on the perspective grid for lists, prices and quotes; captions in slanted neon boxes.
Accent one word per phrase in magenta; keep text short and uppercase.

name: Visualshot
description: Explainer: big bold centered captions, black-and-white line diagrams, punch-in cuts
guide: Captions carry the video: huge, uppercase, centered, one or two words at a time, the key word in yellow.
Explain every idea with a black full-frame Line Diagram (venn, one to many, growth, cycle, small vs big, stairs) while it is said.
Jump-cut punch-ins every ~2 s; no texture, no color besides the yellow.
Open with a centered full-frame title in the line-art look. Use centered diagrams for the explanation, then return to the speaker. Do not use a split header for this opening.

name: Rewind
description: 90s home video: VHS grade and noise, a TV set, VCR blue-screen menus, closed captions

camera.grade: saturate(1.3) contrast(1.08) sepia(0.2) hue-rotate(-8deg) brightness(1.05) blur(0.5px)

guide: Feels like a tape from 1996: the footage is graded warm and soft, with noise, a rolling tracking band and the camcorder display.
Open with the speaker on a 90s TV set under a Bungee title (Hook Card tv).
Lists and numbers as VCR blue-screen menus; counts as a TV volume bar.
Captions as closed captions: white on black boxes, the spoken word in yellow.

name: Lumen
description: Clean: Inter on soft dark cards, one blue accent, a slow push-in
guide: Calm: one overlay every 5–8 s, never two at once; the camera pushes in slowly.
Open with the speaker as a rounded inset under a centered title (Hook Card inset).
Cards float over the footage rather than covering it.
Accent one word per title at most.

name: Signal
description: Direct business advice: charcoal, lime emphasis, bold captions and clear proof.
guide: First transcribe the source with agentcut_transcribe. Review word timings and listen before removing dead air, repeated takes or filler words. Keep breaths, intentional pauses and the meaning of each sentence. Do not remove speech from transcript guesses alone.
Build the speech edit first with source trims and split clips. Close the resulting gaps and remap captions, B-roll and audio to the edited timeline. Keep the source files unchanged.

Review the picture about every 4–6 seconds for a useful change at a new idea, example or emphasis. Use a modest punch-in, wider reset or relevant B-roll only when it helps. Never insert cuts on a fixed five-second timer. The preset leaves the camera still so shot-level edits control the framing.

Use only supplied or approved B-roll and licensed audio. If footage is missing, use a useful text or diagram insert. Keep speech clear above music; measure the mix and check cuts for clicks. A color filter does not restore missing detail or upscale footage.
Lead with one useful claim, support it with an example, then give the next action. Keep the speaker prominent. Avoid decorative transitions and constant stickers.

Use short three-word caption groups, with lime on the key word. Use one stat counter for a real number and a compact list for actionable steps. Prefer straight cuts; return to the wider shot after an emphasis.
Keep skin tones neutral and the backdrop quiet. Use a low, steady music bed only if it helps; silence is valid for direct advice.

Open over full-frame footage with a compact left-aligned title card in the lower third (hook-card layout:card, position:lower, align:left). Keep it below the face and above the bottom safe zone; hide captions during this title.

name: Studyroom
description: Warm lessons: cream pages, teal notes, calm type and clear chapter cards.

Organize the lesson into a question, a worked example and a short recap. Keep natural thinking pauses; remove only delays that do not help comprehension.
Use warm cream chapter cards with teal emphasis, a rounded speaker inset and six-word caption lines. Show screen recordings or diagrams during the explanation, then return to the face.
Apply only a slight warm grade after checking white balance. Use soft music and sparse, quiet reveal sounds. Let each example stay visible long enough to read.

name: Afterglow
description: Product stories: dark plum, copper titles, detail shots and restrained motion.
guide: First transcribe the source with agentcut_transcribe. Review word timings and listen before removing dead air, repeated takes or filler words. Keep breaths, intentional pauses and the meaning of each sentence. Do not remove speech from transcript guesses alone.

Build a short product story: reveal, useful detail, demonstration, payoff. Keep the voice edit clean and use supplied close-ups to show the claim.
Alternate wide, detail and action shots at meaningful beats. Use match cuts where the source supports them. Use a brief light leak only at a scene change; avoid a transition on every cut.
Use large copper serif titles with generous empty space. Reserve captions for spoken explanation. Keep highlights below clipping and avoid heavy orange skin tones.
Place music hits and subtle source-backed Foley on actual actions. Do not add fake product sounds or claim speed ramps without source frames and an explicit timeline edit.

name: Fieldnote
description: Documentary notes: ivory serif titles, rust markers, source cards and light grain.
guide: First transcribe the source with agentcut_transcribe. Review word timings and listen before removing dead air, repeated takes or filler words. Keep breaths, intentional pauses and the meaning of each sentence. Do not remove speech from transcript guesses alone.
Build the speech edit first with source trims and split clips. Close the resulting gaps and remap captions, B-roll and audio to the edited timeline. Keep the source files unchanged.

Build a setup, a question or conflict, and a supported resolution. Preserve pauses that carry emotion. Use captions as access to the speech, not as invented narration.
Use ivory serif chapter titles, rust markers and source labels. Show evidence as supplied images or screen recordings, with a clear source caption. Never invent a quote, date, map or statistic.
Use a wider speaker frame for context and a modest closer crop for a personal point. Hold on documents long enough to read. Use light grain and neutral color; preserve natural room tone.
Use quote cards only for exact verified words. Keep music sparse under testimony, and finish with the answer to the opening question rather than an unrelated call to action.
Open with a centered, full-frame ivory serif chapter card, not torn paper, tape or collage. Cut to the speaker once the question is clear. Keep rust markers small and evidence cards square and quiet.
